properties.name: Mahabharata — Kurukshetra War
properties.summary: The great war between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins for the throne of Hastinapura lasted eighteen days. Krishna served as Arjuna's charioteer, delivering the Bhagavad Gita on the battlefield. The Pandavas won but at devastating cost, with almost all warriors dead. The epic addresses dharma, duty, and cosmic justice.

properties.name: Ramayana — Rama's Journey
properties.summary: Prince Rama was exiled for fourteen years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. The demon king Ravana abducted Sita to Lanka. Rama allied with Hanuman and the monkey army, built a bridge across the ocean, and defeated Ravana. He returned to Ayodhya as king, celebrated as the festival Diwali.

properties.name: Churning of the Ocean of Milk
properties.summary: Devas and Asuras cooperated to churn the cosmic ocean using Mount Mandara as a churning rod and Vasuki the serpent as a rope. From the ocean emerged treasures: Lakshmi, the divine physician, the moon, and the elixir of immortality (amrita). Vishnu as Mohini tricked the Asuras to ensure only the Devas drank the amrita.

properties.name: Manu and the Great Flood
properties.summary: Manu, the first man, found a small fish that was Vishnu's avatar Matsya. The fish warned of a coming flood and instructed Manu to build a boat. When the flood came, Matsya grew enormous and towed the boat to safety on a mountain peak. Manu repopulated the earth through sacrifice and prayer.

properties.name: Krishna's Divine Play (Lila)
properties.summary: Born in a prison to defeat the tyrant Kamsa, Krishna was raised among cowherds. He performed miracles — lifting Mount Govardhana, dancing with the gopis, and playing enchanting flute. His love with Radha represents the soul's longing for the divine. He later served as Arjuna's charioteer in the Mahabharata.

properties.name: Pralaya — Cosmic Dissolution
properties.summary: Hindu cosmology envisions vast cycles of creation and destruction. Each cosmic day of Brahma (kalpa) spans 4.32 billion years. At the end, Shiva dances the Tandava, dissolving the universe. Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic serpent Shesha in primordial waters. From his navel grows a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates anew.

properties.name: Purusha Sacrifice — Vedic Creation
properties.summary: The cosmic being Purusha was sacrificed by the gods. From his body, the world was created: his mouth became brahmins, arms became warriors, thighs became merchants, feet became servants. From his mind came the moon, eyes the sun, breath the wind. This primordial sacrifice established cosmic and social order.

properties.name: Narasimha — The Man-Lion Avatar
properties.summary: The demon king Hiranyakashipu received a boon: he could not be killed by man or animal, inside or outside, by day or night. He terrorized his devoted son Prahlada who worshipped Vishnu. Vishnu appeared as Narasimha (half-man, half-lion) at twilight, on a threshold, and killed the demon on his lap.

properties.name: The Birth of Ganesha
properties.summary: Parvati created a boy from turmeric paste to guard her bath. When Shiva returned and the boy blocked him, Shiva beheaded him in rage. Parvati's grief was so great that Shiva promised to restore the child with the head of the first creature found — an elephant. Thus Ganesha was born, remover of obstacles and lord of beginnings.

properties.name: Shiva's Cosmic Dance (Nataraja)
properties.summary: Shiva performs the Tandava, the cosmic dance that creates, sustains, and destroys the universe. As Nataraja (Lord of the Dance), he dances within a ring of fire. One foot crushes the dwarf Apasmara (ignorance), while the other is raised in liberation. His drum sounds creation, his fire hand destruction.

properties.name: Durga Slays Mahishasura
properties.summary: The buffalo demon Mahishasura received a boon that he could be killed by no god or man. He conquered the heavens. The gods combined their energies to create Durga, a goddess of supreme power. Each god gave her a weapon. After a nine-day battle, she slew Mahishasura, proving that divine feminine power surpasses all.

properties.name: Hanuman's Leap to Lanka
properties.summary: The monkey god Hanuman, son of Vayu (Wind), volunteered to leap across the ocean to Lanka to find the captured Sita. He overcame Surasa, a sea demoness, and Simhika who tried to catch his shadow. He found Sita, delivered Rama's ring, set Lanka ablaze with his burning tail, and returned triumphant.
